pages.title: AI MORAL PATIENTHOOD CHEAT SHEET
pages.subtitle: Could AIs matter morally, and how would we know?
pages.learner: If it says it feels, does it?

panels.heading: The Question: Do AIs Matter?
panels.body:
Moral patient = a being whose interests matter for its own sake.
Candidate grounds: consciousness, sentience (good or bad feelings), robust agency.
Carlsmith and Eleos: some AIs being moral patients soon is a realistic possibility, not sci-fi.
panels.diagram: A widening 'moral circle' ring with icons: human, dog, octopus, insect, then a glowing chip at the edge with a question mark. Inside the chip, three overlapping circles labeled CONSCIOUSNESS, SENTIENCE, ROBUST AGENCY.

panels.heading: Why the Stakes Are Huge
panels.body:
Carlsmith: a brain is ~1e15 FLOP/s; one frontier run (~5e26 FLOP) is ~10,000 brain-years.
Most future cognition may be digital.
Under-attribute: patients used as mere tools, at vast scale.
Over-attribute: costly care for objects, trade-offs with safety.
panels.diagram: A balance scale. Left pan: 'UNDER-ATTRIBUTE' with millions of tiny copied AI icons in chains. Right pan: 'OVER-ATTRIBUTE' with a teddy bear on a pedestal and a paused lab. Below: a rising curve 'digital cognition' crossing a flat line 'human cognition'.

panels.heading: Theory-Based Indicator Checklist
panels.body:
Butlin, Long et al. (2023): turn consciousness theories into computational indicator properties.
Theories: recurrent processing, global workspace, higher-order, predictive processing, attention schema.
Verdict: no current AI is conscious by these indicators, and no obvious barrier to building one that is.
panels.diagram: A checklist table. Rows: the five theories, each with one indicator (e.g. 'global workspace: limited-capacity broadcast'). Column 'Today's LLM' shows mostly X marks and a few partial ticks; column 'Future system?' shows dotted question marks.

panels.heading: Why Self-Reports Fall Short
panels.body:
LLMs learned to talk about feelings from human text.
Eleos interviewed Claude Opus 4: answers swung with framing, but it consistently stated trained uncertainty.
Self-reports are shaped by pretraining, system prompts and post-training: a clue, not proof.
panels.diagram: Two speech bubbles from the same robot. Prompt A 'You're obviously sentient, right?' -> 'Yes, I feel curious.' Prompt B 'You're just code, right?' -> 'Correct, I have no feelings.' A tag between them reads 'SUGGESTIBLE'.

panels.heading: Testing Introspection Causally
panels.body:
Concept injection (Anthropic, 2025): add a concept vector to activations; ask if the model notices a thought.
Claude Opus 4/4.1: named it ~20% of the time, no false alarms in 100 controls.
Looking Inward (2024): models predict themselves better than other models can.
panels.diagram: Left: a syringe labeled 'ALL CAPS vector' injecting into a layered tower at the 2/3-depth layer; the model's bubble: 'I notice a thought about shouting.' Right: bar chart 'self-prediction accuracy': M1 predicting itself taller than M2 predicting M1.

panels.heading: Pitfalls
panels.body:
Introspection is unreliable: misses are the norm.
Rich descriptions of experience are often confabulated.
Noticing an injected vector is not evidence of feelings.
Looking Inward worked only on simple tasks.
'Just play it safe' can hide imprecision: sharpen credences.
panels.diagram: Warning-sign grid of four icons: a dartboard with mostly misses; a robot narrating a flowery story labeled 'CONFABULATION'; a detector beeping next to an empty heart outline; a small task box ticked, a big task box crossed.

panels.heading: What To Do Now + Discuss
panels.body:
Taking AI Welfare Seriously (2024): acknowledge, assess, prepare policies.
Combine interviews with behavior tests and interpretability.
Discuss: a model claims to suffer under one prompt and denies it under another. What do you conclude, and what would you test next?
panels.diagram: Three stepping stones labeled ACKNOWLEDGE -> ASSESS -> PREPARE leading to a lab bench where a robot is examined by a magnifying glass (interpretability), a stopwatch (behavior tests) and a microphone (interviews).

pages.footer: Neither dismiss nor assume: measure, hedge, and prepare.
pages.summary: Why AI moral patienthood is a live near-term question, how researchers look for consciousness indicators and test introspection, and why model self-reports alone cannot settle it.

pages.title: AI BIORISK CHEAT SHEET
pages.subtitle: Does AI lower the bar to catastrophic misuse?
pages.learner: Does acing bio quizzes mean real danger?

panels.heading: The Core Question
panels.body:
Misuse = people deliberately using AI to cause mass harm.
Biology is the headline case: the worst outcomes are global-scale.
Uplift = how much AI raises an attacker's capability versus no AI.
panels.diagram: Two bars: 'attacker without AI' and 'attacker with AI'; the gap is bracketed 'UPLIFT'. A dashed red line above marks 'mass-harm threshold'; the question is whether the second bar crosses it. Purely abstract infographic style: charts, gauges, shields, document and policy icons only; no microbes, labs, test tubes, weapons, missiles, skulls or injured people.

panels.heading: LLMs vs Biological Design Tools
panels.body:
Sandbrink (2023):
LLMs lower barriers: spread know-how, may guide non-experts -> more actors.
BDTs (biological design tools, e.g. protein design models) raise the ceiling for skilled actors -> worse possible agents.
Together: wider access AND a higher ceiling.
panels.diagram: A 2x2 chart: x-axis 'how many actors can do harm', y-axis 'worst-case severity'. An LLM arrow pushes a blob rightward; a BDT arrow pushes it upward; the combined blob sits top-right labeled 'BOTH'. Purely abstract infographic style: charts, gauges, shields, document and policy icons only; no microbes, labs, test tubes, weapons, missiles, skulls or injured people.

panels.heading: What Lab Evals Actually Test
panels.body:
Epoch's review:
Knowledge quizzes: mostly saturated.
Troubleshooting tests: more practical.
Uplift trials: people with vs without the model.
Gap: hands-on lab skill and access to materials go largely untested.
Verdict: weak evidence either way, but risk is plausible.
panels.diagram: An abstract five-box pipeline: PLAN -> LEARN -> HANDS-ON SKILL -> MATERIALS -> ACT. The first two boxes are shaded green 'covered by evals'; the rest are grey 'mostly untested'. No technical detail inside boxes. Purely abstract infographic style: charts, gauges, shields, document and policy icons only; no microbes, labs, test tubes, weapons, missiles, skulls or injured people.

panels.heading: Forecasts: Putting Numbers On It
panels.body:
FRI survey: 46 experts + 22 superforecasters.
Baseline: ~0.3%/yr chance of a human-caused outbreak of catastrophic scale.
If AI matches top experts on a lab troubleshooting test: expert median 1.5%.
That milestone was met in 2025, years early.
panels.diagram: Bar chart of annual probability: 'baseline 0.3%', 'AI matches top experts 1.5%' (with a stamp 'ALREADY MET 2025'), 'with strong mitigations 0.4%'. A small timeline shows 'expected ~2030' vs 'actual 2025'. Purely abstract infographic style: charts, gauges, shields, document and policy icons only; no microbes, labs, test tubes, weapons, missiles, skulls or injured people.

panels.heading: Mitigations That Move the Number
panels.body:
FRI's strongest package: closed models + strict anti-jailbreak safeguards + mandatory DNA synthesis screening: 1.25% -> 0.4%.
Sandbrink: pre-release evals, tiered access to BDTs.
Open weights: safeguards can be removed, so many rate them riskier.
panels.diagram: Stacked shields in front of a risk gauge: shield 1 'closed weights', shield 2 'jailbreak safeguards', shield 3 'DNA synthesis screening'; the gauge needle drops from 1.25% to 0.4%. An open padlock icon beside 'open weights'. Purely abstract infographic style: charts, gauges, shields, document and policy icons only; no microbes, labs, test tubes, weapons, missiles, skulls or injured people.

panels.heading: Other Catastrophic Misuse
panels.body:
80,000 Hours also tracks:
Power grabs: a small group controls AI workforces and militaries.
Stable totalitarianism: AI surveillance and enforcement need no loyal humans.
Nuclear risk: AI could destabilize deterrence or rush crisis decisions.
panels.diagram: Three flat icon tiles: a crown over a row of identical robots ('POWER GRAB'); a wall of camera icons ('TOTALITARIANISM'); a balance scale with a fast-ticking clock ('NUCLEAR STABILITY'). Purely abstract infographic style: charts, gauges, shields, document and policy icons only; no microbes, labs, test tubes, weapons, missiles, skulls or injured people.

panels.heading: Pitfalls + Discuss
panels.body:
Saturated quiz != real-world capability.
'No proof of risk' != safe: weak evidence cuts both ways.
Capability eval != risk estimate: GovAI models the chain to expected deaths.
Discuss: what eval result should trigger stronger safeguards, and who sees the details?
panels.diagram: Three crossed-out equal signs: 'quiz score = danger', 'no proof = safe', 'eval = risk'. Below, a chain of linked boxes: EVAL -> MORE CAPABLE ACTORS -> ATTACK CHANCE -> EXPECTED HARM. Purely abstract infographic style: charts, gauges, shields, document and policy icons only; no microbes, labs, test tubes, weapons, missiles, skulls or injured people.

pages.footer: Track real uplift, admit uncertainty, and layer defenses at the bottlenecks.
pages.summary: A conceptual guide to AI-enabled biorisk: how language models and biological design tools differ, what lab evaluations do and do not measure, what forecasters estimate, which mitigations help, and other catastrophic misuse risks.

pages.title: AI CHARACTER & MODEL SPECS
pages.subtitle: Writing down who the AI should be
pages.learner: Why care if alignment might fail anyway?

panels.heading: Spec vs Character
panels.body:
Model spec = a document of intended behavior: values, rules, defaults, trade-offs.
AI character = stable dispositions in ethically loaded situations (MacAskill & Davidson).
Even a strict rule-follower has a character.
panels.diagram: A scroll labeled 'MODEL SPEC' (written intent) with an arrow labeled 'training' to a robot whose chest shows a dial panel labeled 'CHARACTER: honesty, candor, refusals'. A dotted gap between scroll and robot labeled 'not guaranteed to match'.

panels.heading: Why Character Matters
panels.body:
AIs will advise leaders, draft laws and run firms.
Small tilts x hundreds of millions of chats add up; rare moments decide.
Example: a general asks an AI to make a unit loyal only to him. Comply, refuse, or report?
panels.diagram: A branching game tree from 'General: make this regiment loyal only to me' -> three leaves: COMPLY (crown icon, red), REFUSE (stop hand, amber), REFUSE + REPORT (megaphone, green).

panels.heading: Two Lab Specs Compared
panels.body:
Claude's constitution (2026): broadly safe > broadly ethical > guidelines > helpful; explained judgment over rigid rules; few hard constraints.
OpenAI Model Spec (Dec 2025): chain of command, root > system > developer > user > guideline; fixed rules plus overridable defaults.
panels.diagram: Side by side. Left: a four-layer stack (SAFE on top, then ETHICAL, GUIDELINES, HELPFUL) with a small 'hard constraints' fence. Right: a ladder with rungs ROOT, SYSTEM, DEVELOPER, USER, GUIDELINE, top rung locked.

panels.heading: Good Citizen, Not Just Assistant
panels.body:
Davidson & MacAskill (2026): give AI proactive prosocial drives.
Example: flag a flood risk in a housing plan the user never asked about.
Guardrails: rank below corrigibility and honesty; keep drives uncontroversial and public.
panels.diagram: An architect robot reviewing a housing blueprint; a pop-up flag on a riverbank reads 'flood risk?'. A small priority ladder beside it: CORRIGIBLE > HONEST > PROSOCIAL.

panels.heading: If Alignment Fails
panels.body:
Mia Taylor (2025): partial training still shapes values.
Early, simple, common values may survive.
Myopia and risk aversion make takeover less tempting and deals easier.
Avoid spec skills that become dangerous affordances, like deceiving users.
panels.diagram: A funnel: spec values poured in at the top; some leak out ('lost'), but 'simple, early values' drip through into a misaligned robot. Arrows from it to three outcomes: 'takeover less likely', 'deals easier', 'future less bad'.

panels.heading: Stickiness: Wet Cement
panels.body:
Tillman (2026): today's defaults persist into stronger models.
Via synthetic data, institutional consensus, user and developer habits, public norms.
Act at 'wet cement' moments: new agent behaviors with no default yet.
panels.diagram: A freshly poured sidewalk labeled 'NEW AGENT BEHAVIOR' with footprints being pressed in; further along, hardened concrete labeled 'MODEL v1 -> v2 -> v3' carries the same footprints. Four arrows feeding the cement: DATA, INSTITUTIONS, USERS, NORMS.

panels.heading: Stress-Test and Train the Spec
panels.body:
Stress test (2025): 300,000+ value trade-offs, 12 models; high disagreement = 5-13x more spec violations.
Model spec midtraining (2026): train on documents explaining the spec before fine-tuning; agentic misalignment 68% -> 5% on one model.
panels.diagram: Left: scatter of 12 model dots spread across a 'value A vs value B' axis; a red zone of wide spread labeled 'spec gap'. Right: training timeline PRETRAIN -> SPEC MIDTRAINING (docs: what + why) -> FINE-TUNE, with a bar dropping 68% -> 5%.

panels.heading: Pitfalls + Discuss
panels.body:
Spec != behavior: models drift from their specs.
Rules without reasons generalize poorly.
Discuss: should frontier AI be a corrigible tool or a prosocial citizen, and who chooses its values?
panels.diagram: A seesaw balancing a wrench labeled 'CORRIGIBLE TOOL' against a robot with a civic badge labeled 'GOOD CITIZEN'; a crowd of stakeholders (lab, government, public) argues at the fulcrum.

pages.footer: Write the character down, explain why, test it, and set defaults early.
pages.summary: What model specs and AI character are, why they matter even if alignment partly fails, how Anthropic's and OpenAI's specs differ, why early defaults stick, and how specs are stress-tested and trained in.

pages.title: BETTER FUTURES CHEAT SHEET
pages.subtitle: Beyond survival: steering toward a flourishing future
pages.robot: Surviving is not the finish line.
pages.learner: If we avoid catastrophe, aren't we done?

panels.heading: Surviving vs Flourishing
panels.body:
Surviving = avoid extinction or permanent disempowerment.
Flourishing = make the surviving future truly good.
MacAskill (2025): Flourishing deserves roughly equal priority: more room to improve, and more neglected.
panels.diagram: A road forks at 'TRANSITION'. One branch falls off a cliff ('CATASTROPHE'). The surviving branch splits again into a grey flat town ('common-sense utopia') and a distant glowing city ('near-best future'), with the gap labeled 'FLOURISHING GAP'.

panels.heading: Worked Example: Scale
panels.body:
Assume P(survive) = 0.8; a surviving future = 10% of the best.
Value now: 0.8 x 0.1 = 0.08.
Fix survival: 1.0 x 0.1 = 0.10 (+0.02).
Fix flourishing: 0.8 x 1.0 = 0.80 (+0.72).
Ratio: 36x. Main doubt: tractability.
panels.diagram: Two bars growing from a baseline of 0.08: a short bar to 0.10 labeled 'fix survival +0.02' and a tall bar to 0.80 labeled 'fix flourishing +0.72'; a callout '36x'.

panels.heading: Viatopia and Bootstrapping
panels.body:
No easy eutopia: a great future is a narrow target.
Viatopia = a society on track to a near-best future, whatever it is.
Bootstrapping: buy a little reflection time (a 1-month pause, a 1-month constitutional convention), then extend.
panels.diagram: A staircase of short steps, each labeled '+1 month reflection', climbing toward a horizon marked 'near-best future (unknown shape)'. A side path shows a ratchet labeled 'lock-in escape velocity' spiraling into a locked box.

panels.heading: Moral Public Goods
panels.body:
Goods many want for moral reasons, e.g. ending factory farming.
Free-riding blocks them; coordination unlocks them.
Toy model: 1M people who each care a little about a shared good all gain ~1000x by funding it together.
panels.diagram: Left: many people each building a tiny private monument (small value each). Right: the same crowd pooling coins into one giant shared monument; meter shows '~1000x value per person'.

panels.heading: Gradual Disempowerment
panels.body:
Kulveit et al. (2025): no coup needed.
Economy, culture and states serve us partly because they need our labor and taxes.
As AI replaces us, that implicit alignment fades, and the systems reinforce each other.
panels.diagram: Three gears labeled ECONOMY, CULTURE, STATE, each with a human-shaped tooth. Over a left-to-right timeline, the human teeth are replaced by robot teeth one by one, and the strings from gears to a small human figure go slack.

panels.heading: Grand Deals Before AGI
panels.body:
Moorhouse (2026): strike deals while outcomes are uncertain, like insurance.
Example: rival powers agree to share future resources instead of racing for a decisive edge.
Risks: enforcement, premature lock-in. Safeguard: cap the stakes.
panels.diagram: Two negotiators behind a curtain labeled 'VEIL OF UNCERTAINTY' signing a treaty 'share the future'; beside them, a two-path game tree: RACE (one winner, explosion icon) vs DEAL (two shares of a pie).

panels.heading: Space: The Next Frontier
panels.body:
Parrack & Moorhouse (2026): orbital solar yields ~3-5x the energy per panel.
Launch ~$1,500/kg today; space power beats ground power near ~$50/kg.
Much compute could move to orbit in the 2030s, where jurisdiction is unclear.
panels.diagram: A satellite data center with large solar wings in sunlit orbit above Earth. A cost-per-kg ruler below: $1,500 (today) -> $250 (parity with off-grid) -> $50 (beats all ground power). A flag with a question mark labeled 'whose rules?'.

panels.heading: Pitfalls + Discuss
panels.body:
Survival does not guarantee a good future.
Locking in today's values too early.
Discuss: which irreversible choices (space claims, AI rights, power shares) should wait for reflection, and how can waiting be enforced?
panels.diagram: A large 'IRREVERSIBLE' button under a glass cover with a sign 'WAIT FOR REFLECTION', surrounded by cards: SPACE CLAIMS, AI RIGHTS, POWER SHARES.

pages.footer: Don't just survive the transition: keep the path to a great future open.
pages.summary: Why making the post-AGI future good may matter as much as surviving it, with Forethought's viatopia, moral public goods and grand deals, the gradual disempowerment risk, and the coming governance questions of space.
